summary_oneline: ParquetSource for MultiQS: read Parquet from local FS, S3 or GCS into a DataFrame, mirroring S3Source

localization.role: base contract: fetch(), resolve_credential, resolve_masks, per-thread loop
generated component schema to add for ParquetSource

claims.text: New sources register in SOURCE_REGISTRY and are dispatched from the YAML `sources:` list by type name
S3Source reads the full object into memory via aioboto3 and parses only CSV/GZ/Excel
No MultiQS source reads Parquet today; pyarrow is used only for writing (ToS3, cache)
There is no GCS client pattern in querysource to reuse
pyarrow and google-cloud-storage are installed only transitively and must be declared (optional extras) before relying on them
ThreadSource runs fetch() in its own thread/event loop, so sync pyarrow reads do not block the aiohttp loop, but wrapping them in asyncio.to_thread keeps the async convention
A component schema generated/ParquetSource.json and unit tests mirroring test_source_s3.py are expected deliverables

unknowns.question: Which I/O layer reads remote parquet?
unknowns.user_answer: pyarrow.fs (S3FileSystem / GcsFileSystem / LocalFileSystem) + pyarrow.parquet/dataset read in asyncio.to_thread

unknowns.question: One ParquetSource with URI/backend selector, or separate classes?
unknowns.user_answer: Separate classes: ParquetFileSource, ParquetS3Source, ParquetGCSSource sharing a common parquet base/mixin

unknowns.question: How are GCS credentials supplied?
unknowns.user_answer: Service-account JSON via navconfig (default GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_FILE / BIGQUERY_CREDENTIALS), fallback to ADC

unknowns.question: Which read features are in scope (columns, filters, partitioned dirs/globs)?
unknowns.user_answer: All in scope: column projection, row filters, directories / partitioned datasets, masks in path

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the pattern (ThreadSource + SOURCE_REGISTRY) is established; the remaining forks are design choices resolved in Q&A.
